history.summary: Right-sized 1,346sqft 4BR in Pasir Ris at $1.798M, sitting just inside the liquid band, with a strong, reliable 6.32%/yr resale CAGR over 163 transactions. PSF 1336 is slightly above the 1299 median but justified by a properly sized family unit with deep demonstrated demand.
history.rating_rationale: Unlike the oversized D18 4BRs in this batch, Livia is sensibly sized (1,346sqft) and priced at $1.798M — the upper edge of the deep $1.8-2.5M buyer band, broadly appealing to upgrading families. 6.32%/yr over a robust 163-txn series is reliable and well above the OCR baseline. PSF 1336 vs 1299 median is a modest ~3% premium, reasonable for the size efficiency. 720m to Pasir Ris MRT (CRL interchange by ~2030) is a real future catalyst. The best-balanced 4BR investment case in the batch.
red_flags: 720m / 9-min walk to MRT
99LH from 2011 — lease decay over a long hold
Slight PSF premium to median (1336 vs 1299)
catalysts: Pasir Ris becomes a CRL interchange (~2030) — connectivity uplift within 720m
$1.798M quantum and efficient 4BR size = broad upgrader demand

history.summary: Listed as a 4-bedroom, but 1,410 sqft is Livia's 3-BEDROOM + STUDY type. The developer's unit mix runs 3BR+S 1,324-1,410 sqft (225 units) and 4BR 1,539 sqft (160 units), and URA rental filings agree: all 52 4BR contracts ever filed at Livia sit in the 1,500-1,600 sqft band, while the 1,400-1,500 band has 12 contracts, every one filed as 3BR. Re-comped against its actual type, $1,367 psf is at or just above the top of what Livia's 3BR+S has cleared in 2026 ($1,322-$1,350 psf) - a full ask, not value. The project itself is sound (92.2% of 564 resales profitable, REALSCORE 4.1, deep buyer pool, CRL interchange ~2030), which is what keeps this Neutral rather than Avoid, but the unit is the weaker format in its own building: Livia's genuine 4BR trades at a HIGHER psf ($1,408-$1,449 in 2026) than the 3BR+S, so the $1.93M here buys the format the market rewards less.
history.rating_rationale: Priced fully for what it actually is. (1) BEDROOM RELABEL: 1,410 sqft is 3BR+study, not 4BR - confirmed independently by the developer's published mix (3BR+S 1,324-1,410, 225 units; 4BR 1,539, 160 units) and by URA rental filings (52/52 4BR contracts at 1,500-1,600 sqft; the 1,400-1,500 band is 12/12 filed 3BR). bed_bands returns 'ok' only because 1,410 falls inside the 12% tolerance below the 1,550 band floor - the known overlap blindspot; the developer mix is the tie-break. (2) VALUE, the axis that actually predicts, is NEGATIVE: mmr psf_value -1.66 and psf_premium_vs_ura_median_pct +2.9% vs Livia's own median. Livia's 3BR+S cleared 2026 at $1,246-$1,350 psf (1,324 sqft: Jan-26 $1.65M, Feb-26 $1.785M, Mar-26 $1.75M, May-26 $1.788M); this ask is $1,367 psf, above the top of that band, and above any price the type has ever printed ($1.86M peak, Jun/Jul-25 high floor). (3) The relative_value -6.9% 'cheap vs age-adjusted D18 median' is an artifact of comparison_basis size_band 1400-1800 with only 8 band peers - that band pools this 3BR+S with D18's genuine 4BR stock, which carries a bedroom-count premium. Two-tier PSF inside one size band; don't credit it. (4) score_1000 746 rests on the de-weighted channels: appreciation +6.97 (trailing 6.32% CAGR), txn_volume +6.0, dev_size +5.74, age_value +5.45, buyer_pool +4.5. Per the backtest priors trailing CAGR has ~0 forward power, so the headline score is strongest exactly where the evidence is weakest. (5) BETTER UNIT IN THE SAME PROJECT: the real 4BR (1,539 sqft) printed Apr-26 at $2,168k/$1,408 psf and $2,230k/$1,449 psf. For ~8-13% more quantum you get a genuine fourth bedroom, +129 sqft, and the project's most liquid layout (30 prints since 2021, 3 in 2026) instead of a variant that has not printed since Mar-24. NOT AN AVOID: the exit record is real and deep (92.2% profitable on 564 resales, 247 of them above 6% annualized, avg holding 6.5yr), OCR region prior is the favourable one, 81 years of lease is ample, and the ask is only ~1-2% over psf parity with the May-26 sibling print - full, not dislocated. Fairly priced is not a reason to buy; it is a reason to pass and take the 4BR, or wait for a 3BR+S nearer $1,320 psf (~$1.86M).
red_flags: MISLABELLED BEDROOM COUNT: advertised 4BR; 1,410 sqft is Livia's 3BR+study type per the developer's unit mix (3BR+S 1,324-1,410 sqft, 225 units) and per 12/12 URA rental contracts in the 1,400-1,500 band filed as 3BR. Zero 4BR contracts (0 of 52) have ever been filed below 1,500 sqft at this project.

bed_bands returns 'ok' only via the 12% tolerance below the 1,550 4BR band floor (1,550 x 0.88 = 1,364 < 1,410) - the overlap blindspot, not a clean pass. The 3BR band (1,250-1,650, 165 contracts) also contains this size.
Ask is above its own type's 2026 clearing band: 3BR+S cleared $1,246-$1,350 psf in 2026; this asks $1,367 psf. No 3BR+S at Livia has ever printed above $1.86M; the ask is $1.928M.

The 1,410 sqft variant specifically has 9 URA prints since Jun-2021 and NONE since Mar-2024 (28 months), while its 1,324 sibling printed 4x in 2026. Exit will be comped against those siblings, which cap around $1,350 psf - a price ceiling, more than an illiquidity problem.

Rent in factual_data is overstated: $5,350/mo was taken from the 4BR 1,500-1,600 sqft band (21 recent contracts). This unit's own band (1,400-1,500) has a $5,000 median across 12 contracts (6 recent). Corrected gross yield ~3.11%, not 3.33%; realsmart's project-level estimate of 3.2% agrees. Net yield ~1.6-1.7%.
relative_value's -6.9% discount uses size_band 1400-1800 with 8 band peers, pooling a 3BR+S against D18's genuine 4BR stock - a two-tier-PSF-within-a-size-band artifact, not value.

Trailing 6.32% CAGR is a single-regime (2021-26 bull) number. Same-size resale pairs confirm it is real rather than a size-mix artifact (1,324 sqft Nov-21 $1,328k -> May-26 $1,788k = 6.8%/yr; 1,539 sqft Nov-21 $1,550k -> Apr-26 $2,230k = 8.6%/yr), but the backtest priors give trailing CAGR ~0 forward power - do not extrapolate it.

Only floor 'low/mid' is knowable - floor_level is null in the feed and Livia has no researched profile, so stack, facing and floor premium are unverified. Livia's own prints show a wide floor spread (1,346 sqft: $1,263 psf at floors 6-10 vs $1,382 psf at 11-15, same month), so this is a material unpriced variable.
99-yr lease from 07/01/2008 - 81 years left. Ample now, but a 5-7yr hold sells at ~74-76 years, the point where the first buyer-financing and CPF frictions start being discussed.

84% of Livia sold at launch in 2008 at ~$700-900 psf, so the 92.2%-profitable record is dominated by launch-to-resale gains banked through the 2021-26 bull. It certifies the project holds value; it does not forecast a 2026 buyer's return at $1,367 psf.
catalysts: Cross Island Line Phase 1 makes Pasir Ris an EWL/CRL interchange ~2030, with a separate Pasir Ris Town CRL station ~2032 (Phase 2) - dated and under construction. Discount it: announced since 2019 and substantially priced, and the repo's own backtest finds the future-infrastructure score has NO measured forward power.

Deep, demonstrated exit book: 564 resales, 92.2% profitable, 520 profitable vs 44 unprofitable, 247 above 6% annualized, avg holding 6.5 years. Well past the 150-resale trust floor - the strongest available downside evidence.
OCR region prior is the favourable one (realized forward OCR +3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%), and D18 buyer-pool depth is 'deep' on a 724-unit development.
Family-estate fundamentals: Elias Park Primary 261m (within 1km), Park View 615m, Meridian 886m; Pasir Ris Park, White Sands and the bus interchange within reach.

Pasir Ris 8 (~480 units, integrated with mall/bus interchange/polyclinic at the MRT) lifts the town centre's amenity level - though it is also a competing, better-located product at the interchange itself.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Adequate carry, not a driver, and thinner than the file states. The correct comp is Livia's 1,400-1,500 sqft rental band - 12 contracts, $5,000/mo median, $5,000 on the 6 recent ones - not the $5,350 the scorer pulled from the 4BR 1,500-1,600 band. At $5,000 on a $1.928M ask that is ~3.11% gross and roughly 1.6-1.7% net after costs and tax; realsmart's independent project estimate of 3.2% (36 contracts, $3.56 avg psf rent) corroborates. Demand itself is genuine and steady - 3BR stock at Livia has 152 filed contracts across the 1,200-1,500 bands, and the 1,300-1,400 band alone shows 20 recent contracts at a $4,700 median, so a landlord will let this unit. But treat the yield strictly as carry: the backtest finds high gross yield predicts LOWER forward price growth (std_beta -0.16), and 3.1% is unremarkable for OCR resale family stock. It neither supports nor undermines the case.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Real past, unremarkable forward. The 6.32% trailing CAGR survives the size-mix test - same-size resale pairs give 6.8%/yr on the 1,324 (Nov-21 $1,328k -> May-26 $1,788k) and 8.6%/yr on the 1,539 (Nov-21 $1,550k -> Apr-26 $2,230k), so this is not a pooled-median artifact. But every one of those pairs sits inside the 2021-26 bull, and the repo's own panel work gives trailing CAGR ~0 marginal forward power once clustered. The forward anchor should be the D18/OCR baseline of ~4.2%/yr, which is why I have overridden the rate down from 6.32% to 4.2% rather than letting the ROI projections compound a bull-regime number for 7 years. Working against even that: the entry is at the top of the type's own clearing band, so the first ~2% of any move is spent getting back to fair value, and the exit is comped against 1,324/1,346 siblings that cap around $1,350 psf. Working for it: OCR is the favourable region, the CRL interchange lands inside a 5-7yr hold, and the project's realized annualized profit over the past year is 4.8%. Net expectation is a market return, not an edge - which is exactly what a Neutral is.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: Unverifiable, and that is itself a caution. floor_level and facing are both null (PropertyGuru does not serve facing at all, and floor is optional for the posting agent), and Livia has no researched profile - stack_profile returns status 'not_researched', so no stack/facing/view join was possible. This matters more than usual here because Livia's own prints show a large floor spread: two 1,346 sqft units sold in the same month at $1,263 psf (floors 6-10) and $1,382 psf (floors 11-15), a 9% gap. The development is 11 blocks of 16 storeys, so there is real high-floor stock to be had. At $1,367 psf this ask is priced as though it were in the upper half; if it turns out to be a low or mid floor the ask is meaningfully full rather than marginally full. Confirm the actual floor and the outlook before any offer, and run /research-development 'Livia' if this project is going to be pursued seriously. On format: the 1,410 is the largest variant of the 3BR+S family, which is the right end of that type to own - but it is still the type the market pays less psf for than the 1,539 4BR.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: D18/OCR measured forward baseline (context.district_appreciation 0.042; realized forward OCR +3.7%/yr on the 28-district panel). The file's 6.32% is resale-to-resale genuine - same-size pairs give 6.8%/yr on the 1,324 and 8.6%/yr on the 1,539 - but it is drawn entirely from the 2021-26 bull, and the repo's own backtest gives trailing CAGR ~0 marginal forward power once clustered. Overriding DOWN to the district baseline so the ROI projections do not compound a single-regime number across a 7-year hold. The CRL interchange (2030/2032) is the dated catalyst that justifies holding at the baseline rather than below it.
